objective: COUNT-BALLS-20261118-001's direction 1 (coordinator's go-ahead, 18 November 2026): every start's sorted row of disagreement counts, read without names, merges grown split bases of two and three orders from seven distinctions, while the full table keeps the orders. Which reading between the two recovers the number of orders k and the lattice dimension: a start's row with its nearest starts' rows, one or full colour refinement of the table, or views of the table within a fixed count of each start; and is there a local one? Exhaustive at n = 7, 8 on the one-split population and the cheapest population to 12, a sample at 9, and proofs about what local readings and colour refinement cannot see. Serves G16 and G1; tests A97. Stays on reading, not growth rules.
status: Complete 2026-11-18 (Successful; referee pending): what the arrangement of the count's rows holds is which start's growth lies at which count from which. One round of colour refinement of the count table (each start's row with every other row tagged by its count) tells apart every one-split grown base through n = 8 (59,675 classes) and every class reached at n = 9 (55,394), so it recovers the number of orders there; the nearest starts' rows nearly do (one merge at n = 8). No local reading does: views need reach 8 to 10 here, and two rings sharing a point give equal views with different orders for every reach (proved); colour refinement fails in general (simplex graphs of C10 and C5 + C5, proved), and k from the full table is NP-hard (classical). 7 of 8 predictions held.
